title: Continuous Relay shield transfer and one shield clock
context: Owner saw repeated SHIELD DOWN / 2s messages, erratic shield animation and refusal to deploy near Relay during a crowded wave. The Relay tap was inside its enemy-targeted attack cadence, crediting only one frame of energy per attack. Shield drain used frame dt but cooldown used the vehicle-motion clock, which can stop independently.
outcome: A pure frame transaction combines continuous Relay/heart input and shield drain. Tiny sub-frame inputs that never sustain a bubble do not report repeated drops. The game gathers nearby Relays every frame independently of enemy targeting, attack cooldown and build downtime; transfer feedback stays at tower cadence. Shield recharge/drain, cooldown, outage and animation now use the gameplay frame clock. Tapped Relays stop attacks and stay offline five seconds after leaving. Restart clears taps and resets rack/station resources. Rates, cap, two-second rack seam and four-second ram combo remain unchanged.
alternatives: Debouncing SHIELD DOWN would hide the repeated energy/drop bug without repairing recharge.
Increasing charge duration or lowering cooldown would change balance instead of correcting the timing owners.
evidence: test/shield-sources.mjs checks 10/30/60/144 Hz charging, net 0.5 s/s from one Relay, one drop after leaving, cooldown recovery, weak inputs and exhausted station remainder.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --shield-perf exercises actual Relay proximity, no enemies, shader visibility, one drop and rack redeploy with a stationary motion clock.
npm test: 73 programs; npm run check; npm run test:browser; npm run build.
The first browser fixture froze an in-progress hull deployment, correctly refusing input; the final fixture waits for deployment to finish before pausing its controlled scenario.
